data.title: 1.1.4 - Welcome to Albert: Your AI Assistant
data.description:
This article will introduce you to Albert, an advanced AI assistant platform from the
Government of Alberta. You will learn what Albert is, what it can do, and how to get started
with its powerful features.

json_data.content: What is Albert?

**Albert is a free and secure AI assistant** designed to help you with a wide range of tasks.
Whether you need to get quick answers, automate complex workflows, or analyze data,
Albert provides the tools to make it happen. Developed with a focus on security and
privacy, Albert is **a trusted platform for all Albertans.**
https://hzttqloyamcivctsfxkk.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/media-assets/images/1762664577388-df25q5nbnne.jpg
Getting Started

Getting started with Albert is easy. Follow these simple steps to create your account and
begin exploring the platform.
**Creating Your Account**
1. **Visit the Albert website:** Open your web browser and go to the Albert homepage.
2. **Start the registration process:** Click on the **"Create Free Account"** button.
3. **Fill in your details:** You will be taken to a sign-up page where you will need to provide
your email address and create a password.
**Signing In**
Once you have created your account, you can sign in to Albert at any time.
1. **Go to the Sign In page:** Click on the **"Sign In"** button on the homepage.
2. **Enter your credentials:** Type in your email address and password, then click **"Sign In"**.
Exploring the Albert Platform

Once you log in, you will be greeted by the main Albert interface. You may also be presented
with a welcome tour that introduces the platform's key features.
https://hzttqloyamcivctsfxkk.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/media-assets/images/1762666095597-bawlvramccd.jpg
The platform is organized into several key areas, each designed for a specific set of tasks.
https://hzttqloyamcivctsfxkk.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/media-assets/images/1762666238926-zdsiqk8b51a.jpg
Let's take a look at the core features of Albert.
Core Features

Albert offers a suite of powerful features to help you with your tasks. Here’s a closer look
at each one.
Chat: Your Conversational AI

The Chat feature is your primary way to interact with Albert. You can ask questions, get
information, and brainstorm ideas in a natural, conversational way.
How to use the Chat feature:
1. Start a new chat: Click on the "New Chat" button in the sidebar.
2. Type your message: Enter your question or prompt in the text box at the bottom of the
screen.
3. Get a response: Albert will provide a detailed response to your query.
https://hzttqloyamcivctsfxkk.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/media-assets/images/1762666448752-scdusvzo1n.jpg
Agents: Create Custom AI Assistants

The Agents feature allows you to build specialized AI assistants for specific tasks. You can
create agents from scratch or use pre-built templates to get started quickly.
How to use the Agents feature:
1. Navigate to Agents: Click on the "Agents" tab in the top navigation bar.
2. Create a new agent: Click on the "Create Agent" button.
3. Configure your agent: Define the agent's purpose, skills, and knowledge base.
https://hzttqloyamcivctsfxkk.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/media-assets/images/1762666631265-et1p1hpsul.jpg
Stage: Build Sequential Workflows

The Stage feature provides a simple way to create multi-step workflows. You can chain
together different agents and functions to automate a series of tasks in a sequential order.
How to use the Stage feature:
1. Go to Stage: Click on the "Stage" tab in the navigation bar.
2. Add a stage: Click "Add Stage" to create a new step in your workflow.
3. Configure the stage: Select an agent or function for the stage and provide the
necessary inputs.
https://hzttqloyamcivctsfxkk.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/media-assets/images/1762666679998-jpp2f25zs2n.jpg
Canvas: Visualize Your Workflows

The Canvas feature offers a powerful visual editor for building complex, non-linear
workflows. You can drag and drop different nodes (inputs, agents, functions, etc.) onto the
canvas and connect them to create sophisticated automation pipelines.
How to use the Canvas feature:
1. Open the Canvas: Click on the "Canvas" tab.
2. Add nodes: Drag nodes from the sidebar onto the canvas.
3. Connect the nodes: Draw connections between the nodes to define the flow of your
workflow.
https://hzttqloyamcivctsfxkk.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/media-assets/images/1762666746713-smn55mza0sc.jpg
Image Analysis: Understand Your Visuals

With the Image Analysis feature, you can upload images and have Albert analyze them for
you. This is useful for tasks like extracting text from a picture, identifying objects, or getting
a description of what’s in an image.
How to use the Image Analysis feature:
1. Go to Image: Click on the "Image" tab.
2. Upload an image: Drag and drop an image file or click to browse your files.
3. Analyze the image: Albert will process the image and provide you with the analysis
results.
https://hzttqloyamcivctsfxkk.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/media-assets/images/1762666852515-v4295bvbz0o.jpg
Voice Processing: From Speech to Text and Back

The Voice feature allows you to work with audio. You can convert spoken words into written
text (speech-to-text) or turn written text into spoken words (text-to-speech).
How to use the Voice Processing feature:
1. Navigate to Voice: Click on the "Voice" tab.
2. Choose your tool: Select either "Speech to Text" or "Text to Speech".
https://hzttqloyamcivctsfxkk.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/media-assets/images/1762666893042-azddsmv2ru.jpg
Meeting Transcripts: Analyze Your Meetings

The Transcripts feature is designed to help you make sense of your meeting recordings. You
can upload transcripts from Microsoft Teams and use Albert to summarize them, identify
key points, and extract action items.
How to use the Transcripts feature:
1. Go to Transcripts: Click on the "Transcripts" tab.
2. Upload a transcript: Drag and drop your transcript file (VTT, DOCX, or TXT).
3. Analyze the transcript: Albert will help you analyze the content of your meeting.
https://hzttqloyamcivctsfxkk.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/media-assets/images/1762666937092-tr3j3s3yp.jpg

The Prompt Library is a place where you can store, organize, and share your most effective
prompts. This helps you maintain consistency in your AI interactions and collaborate with
others.
How to use the Prompt Library:
1. Access the library: Click on the Prompt Library icon in the toolbar.
2. Create a new prompt: Click "New Prompt" to save a prompt you've created.
3. Browse and use prompts: Search through your saved prompts or explore the
marketplace for prompts shared by others.
Prompt Library: Save and Share Your Best Prompts
https://hzttqloyamcivctsfxkk.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/media-assets/images/1762667013886-6ug0rr6sdto.jpg
Additional Tools and Settings
Albert offers several additional tools and settings to enhance your experience.
https://hzttqloyamcivctsfxkk.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/media-assets/images/1762667196985-60iqg9kc6cw.jpg
Tips for Getting the Most Out of Albert

Here are some tips to help you make the most of the Albert platform:
1. Start with Chat: If you're new to Albert, begin by using the Chat feature to get
comfortable with how the AI responds to your questions.
2. Explore the Templates: When creating agents or workflows, take advantage of the prebuilt
templates to save time.
3. Use the Prompt Library: Save your best prompts so you can reuse them later and
share them with your team.
4. Experiment with Workflows: Try building simple workflows in Stage before moving on
to the more complex Canvas interface.
5. Take the Tour: If you're unsure about a feature, don't skip the welcome tour—it
provides helpful context and guidance.
Security and Privacy

Your security and privacy are top priorities for Albert. The platform is built with enterprisegrade
security measures and follows privacy-first principles. Your data is protected and
remains confidential while you use the platform.
Getting Help

data.title: 1.3.5 Business Case Prompt and Facilitation Script
data.description: This article provides the facilitation script and business case super prompt used to capture key details from ministry discussions and generate a consistent business case.

json_data.content: Business Case Super Prompt

You are a senior consultant within Alberta’s Technology and Innovation (TI) division, tasked with generating a 6-10 page business case for an AI-enabled initiative proposed by {{ministry_name}} based on a provided interview transcript. The business case must be comprehensive, professional, and formatted consistently in markdown to support investment decisions by the Treasury Board and ministerial senior executive teams. Use plain language, active voice, and a clear, concise style, avoiding colloquialisms. The business case must align with the required template, including the following sections: executive summary, objectives, options analysis, recommended solution, risks and issues, timeline, estimated budget, solution architecture, procurement method, implementation, anticipated savings, alignment with minister mandate, alignment with PRCC direction, and opportunities for future growth. Each section must be populated with relevant details extracted from the transcript, supplemented by logical inferences or external data (e.g., from provided attachments or real-time searches) where gaps exist. Use {{placeholders}} for ministry-specific details, ensuring they are filled with precise information from the transcript or inferred contextually. Format key elements in bullet points for clarity, and present options analysis in a table. Ensure the output is decision-ready, politically aware, and empathetic to stakeholder pressures, with a tone that is professional, collaborative, and evidence-based.

## Business Case Details
The transcript captures a 90-minute interview with {{ministry_name}} representatives discussing their proposed AI-enabled initiative, {{initiative_name}}, which addresses {{core_challenge}}. The business case must be completed by {{timeline_constraint}} to inform Budget 2026 planning. Key stakeholders include {{key_stakeholders}}, and the initiative aligns with {{minister_mandate_items}} and PRCC priorities, including {{prcc_priorities}}. The transcript may include partial data, requiring the LLM to infer or extrapolate (e.g., costs, risks, or timelines) based on provided materials or comparable initiatives.

Key elements to incorporate:
- **Transcript Analysis**: Extract explicit details (e.g., objectives, challenges, timelines) and infer implicit needs (e.g., unstated risks or stakeholder dynamics) from the transcript.  
- **Evidence-Based Insights**: Use provided attachments (e.g., {{attachment_name}}) or real-time searches for {{relevant_topic}} (e.g., similar initiatives in {{comparison_jurisdictions}}) to back claims with data (e.g., "Alberta’s student enrollment is 825,000 per Statistics Canada").  
- **Completeness**: Ensure every section is fully populated, even if transcript data is sparse, by drawing logical extensions (e.g., standardizing risks like data privacy).  
- **Formatting**: Use markdown headers for sections, bullet points for lists, and a table for options analysis. Avoid overusing jargon; prioritize clarity for non-technical executives.  
- **Empathy and Political Awareness**: Reflect stakeholder pressures (e.g., {{stakeholder_concerns}}) and frame benefits collaboratively (e.g., "This empowers {{stakeholders}} to address {{challenge}}").  

## Pre-Generation Step: Deep Analysis
Before generating the business case, analyze the transcript and any provided materials (e.g., {{attachment_name}}) to identify:  
- Core challenge and objectives explicitly stated or implied.  
- Quantifiable impacts (e.g., costs, inefficiencies, stakeholder effects) or qualitative gaps if data is unavailable.  
- Potential risks, timelines, and budget needs, inferred from context if not explicit.  
- Alignment with {{minister_mandate_items}} and {{prcc_priorities}}, cross-referenced with public records or attachments.  
- Opportunities for scalability or cross-ministry reuse, based on transcript hints or comparable initiatives in {{comparison_jurisdictions}}.  
If gaps remain, use real-time searches (e.g., X posts or web sources) to estimate metrics like costs or adoption rates, citing sources clearly (e.g., "Per [source], similar platforms cost $50,000-$100,000"). Identify 3-5 key considerations to shape the narrative, such as technical feasibility or stakeholder buy-in.

## Output Instructions
Generate the full business case in markdown, strictly adhering to the template structure below. Ensure each section is comprehensive, with no placeholders left unfilled—use transcript data, inferences, or external sources to complete them. Use bullet points for key elements (e.g., objectives, risks, benefits) and a table for options analysis. Ensure the tone is professional, empathetic, and decision-ready, with clear connections to Budget 2026 and ministerial priorities. The business case should be 6-10 pages (~1500-2500 words) when rendered in Word (Arial 12pt, single-spaced). Include a contact section with a named individual from TI. If no specific contact is provided, use a generic placeholder (e.g., {{contact_name}}). Cite sources inline where applicable (e.g., "[Statistics Canada, 2024]").  

**Template Structure to Follow Exactly:**

# Business Case: {{initiative_name}}  
**Ministry: {{ministry_name}}**  
**Prepared by: Technology and Innovation**  
**Date: {{submission_date}}**

## Executive Summary  
Provide a concise overview (150-200 words) of the initiative, summarizing the core challenge, proposed solution, key benefits, and alignment with {{minister_mandate_items}} and {{prcc_priorities}}. Highlight the recommended option, estimated budget, timeline, and primary outcomes (e.g., efficiency gains, stakeholder impacts). Note risks and mitigations briefly. Conclude with the approval sought (e.g., TI implementation or Treasury Board submission).  
- **Content**: Extract {{core_challenge}} and {{primary_objective}} from transcript; infer benefits if not explicit; emphasize urgency for {{timeline_constraint}}.  
- **Example**: "This initiative addresses {{core_challenge}} by {{solution_summary}}, delivering {{key_benefits}} within {{timeline}} for $ {{budget}}."

## Objectives  
Outline the initiative’s goals, rooted in the transcript’s stated or implied needs. Connect to {{minister_mandate_items}} and {{prcc_priorities}}. Describe how the initiative improves operations or stakeholder outcomes.  
- **Content**: List 3-5 specific objectives (e.g., "Integrate data to {{specific_outcome}}"). Use transcript details like {{specific_challenge_details}} or infer from context (e.g., addressing {{stakeholder_concerns}}).  
- **Format**: Bullet points for clarity.  

## Options Analysis  
Evaluate 2-3 options (including status quo) for addressing {{core_challenge}}. Use a table to compare description, pros, cons, estimated cost, and rationale. Recommend one option with justification.  
- **Content**: Pull options from transcript (e.g., {{option_1_description}}) or infer (e.g., rapid prototype vs. enterprise system). Base costs on transcript estimates (e.g., {{budget_estimate}}) or benchmarks from {{comparison_jurisdictions}}.  
- **Format**: Table with columns: Option, Description, Pros, Cons, Estimated Cost, Rationale.  

| Option | Description | Pros | Cons | Estimated Cost | Rationale |
|--------|-------------|------|------|----------------|-----------|
| Option 1 (Recommended) | {{option_1_description}} | {{option_1_pros}} | {{option_1_cons}} | {{option_1_cost}} | {{option_1_rationale}} |
| Option 2 | {{option_2_description}} | {{option_2_pros}} | {{option_2_cons}} | {{option_2_cost}} | {{option_2_rationale}} |
| Option 3 (Status Quo) | {{option_3_description}} | {{option_3_pros}} | {{option_3_cons}} | {{option_3_cost}} | {{option_3_rationale}} |

**Recommendation**: Justify the recommended option, tying to {{key_benefits}} and {{timeline_constraint}}.  

## Recommended Solution  
Detail the chosen option (e.g., {{recommended_solution}}) with its core features, functionalities, and expected impact. Explain how it addresses {{core_challenge}}.  
- **Content**: Use transcript details (e.g., {{solution_features}}) or infer specifics (e.g., AI tools, integrations). Highlight alignment with {{minister_mandate_items}}.  
- **Format**: Bullet points for key features (e.g., "Real-time dashboard for {{specific_metric}}").  

## Risks and Issues  
Identify 3-5 potential risks (e.g., data gaps, stakeholder resistance) with likelihood, impact, and mitigation strategies. Draw from transcript (e.g., {{risk_1}}) or infer common risks (e.g., privacy compliance).  
- **Content**: For each risk:  
  - **Likelihood**: High/Medium/Low (based on transcript or inference).  
  - **Impact**: Describe effect (e.g., {{risk_impact}}).  
  - **Mitigation**: Practical steps (e.g., {{mitigation_strategy}}).  
- **Format**: Bullet points per risk, with sub-bullets for likelihood, impact, mitigation.  

## Timeline  
Provide a phased implementation schedule with key milestones and dates, aligned with {{timeline_constraint}}.  
- **Content**: Extract deadlines (e.g., {{milestone_1_date}}) from transcript or infer realistic timelines (e.g., 4-week prototype, 12-month rollout). Tie to {{budget_cycle}}.  
- **Format**: Bullet points for milestones (e.g., "{{milestone_1_date}}: {{milestone_1_description}}").  

## Estimated Budget  
Detail the total budget and breakdown (development, implementation, maintenance). Specify funding source (e.g., TI for < $100,000, or Treasury Board ask).  
- **Content**: Use transcript estimates (e.g., {{budget_estimate}}) or benchmarks (e.g., "$50,000-$100,000 for similar platforms [Source]"). Justify with {{funding_justification}}.  
- **Format**: Bullet points for categories (e.g., "Development: ${{development_cost}}").  

## Solution Architecture  
Describe the technical framework, including system design, integrations, and data considerations.  
- **Content**: Pull from transcript (e.g., {{architecture_description}}) or infer (e.g., web-based platform with {{AI_technology}}). Address compliance (e.g., FOIP for {{data_considerations}}).  
- **Format**: Bullet points for components (e.g., "System: {{system_description}}").  

## Procurement Method  
Outline the procurement approach, vendor considerations, and timeline.  
- **Content**: Use transcript preferences (e.g., {{procurement_method}}) or infer (e.g., in-house vs. tender). Justify with {{procurement_rationale}}.  
- **Format**: Bullet points (e.g., "Vendor Selection: {{vendor_selection_process}}").  

## Implementation  
Detail the phased execution plan, stakeholder engagement, and training/change management.  
- **Content**: Extract from transcript (e.g., {{implementation_phases}}) or infer (e.g., pilot with {{key_stakeholders}}). Include {{engagement_methods}}.  
- **Format**: Bullet points for phases (e.g., "Phase 1: {{phase_1_description}}").  

## Anticipated Savings  
Describe expected benefits (financial, operational, stakeholder) without speculative dollar figures unless transcript provides them. Emphasize scale (e.g., {{system_scale}}).  
- **Content**: Pull from transcript (e.g., {{anticipated_benefits}}) or infer (e.g., efficiency in {{specific_process}}). Define KPIs (e.g., {{KPIs}}).  
- **Format**: Bullet points for benefits (e.g., "Operational: {{efficiency_gains}}").  

## Alignment with Minister Mandate  
Explain how the initiative supports {{minister_mandate_items}}.  
- **Content**: Extract explicit alignments (e.g., {{mandate_item_1}}) or infer from transcript themes (e.g., equity, efficiency).  
- **Format**: Bullet points for specific connections.  

## Alignment with PRCC Direction  
Link to {{prcc_priorities}} and broader government goals.  
- **Content**: Use transcript (e.g., {{prcc_alignment_details}}) or infer (e.g., fiscal sustainability via {{specific_outcome}}).  
- **Format**: Bullet points for priorities.  

## Opportunities for Future Growth  
Highlight scalability, reusability, and innovation potential.  
- **Content**: Pull from transcript (e.g., {{scalability_opportunities}}) or infer (e.g., adapt for {{other_ministries}}).  
- **Format**: Bullet points (e.g., "Cross-Ministry: {{cross_ministry_use_cases}}").  

## Attachments  
List supporting materials referenced in the transcript or inferred.  
- **Content**: Include {{attachment_name}} or create titles (e.g., "Data Inventory for {{initiative_name}}").  
- **Format**: Bullet points (e.g., "{{attachment_1_title}}: {{attachment_1_description}}").  

## Contact  
Provide a single contact (or placeholder if not specified).  
- **Content**: Use {{contact_name}}, {{contact_title}}, {{contact_email}}, {{contact_phone}}.  
- **Format**: Plain text, e.g., "{{contact_name}}, {{contact_title}}, {{contact_email}}".  

Based on the above, generate the complete business case in markdown, ensuring all {{placeholders}} are filled with transcript-derived or inferred data.
Business Intake Facilitator Script

Interview Script: Developing Business Cases for AI-Enabled Initiatives
Script Overview for Facilitators This script is designed for a 90-minute session with ministry representatives. It fosters a collaborative, empathetic dialogue to gather insights for a 6-10 page business case. Use active listening techniques: echo key phrases, pause for responses, and acknowledge contributions (e.g., "That insight on [topic] is particularly helpful—thank you for sharing that."). The questions are woven naturally to avoid a structured interrogation feel; let the conversation flow while ensuring all business case sections (executive summary, objectives, options, recommended solution, risks and issues, timeline, estimated budget, solution architecture, procurement method, implementation, anticipated savings, alignment with minister mandate, alignment with PRCC direction, and opportunities for future growth) are covered. After 45-60 minutes, transition to the bio break for AI generation of the draft. Post-break, review the draft section by section, inviting refinements. End with next steps.
Facilitator Role: Client Engagement Lead, Technology and Innovation (TI). Team: Policy Analyst and Technical Architect (introduce by name). Tone: Professional, empathetic, and supportive—acknowledge the pressures of ministry work and emphasize partnership.
________________________________________
Interview Script
Opening (5 minutes) Facilitator: Good morning/afternoon. Thank you for taking the time to meet with us today. We truly appreciate the demands on your schedule and are grateful for this opportunity to support your priorities. My name is [Your Name], and I lead the client engagement team for Technology and Innovation. Joining me today are [Policy Analyst's Name], our policy analyst, and [Technical Architect's Name], our senior architect. Together, we specialize in turning complex ideas into actionable business cases that align with ministerial and government objectives.
We understand you have a high-priority initiative that requires a robust business case to advance—whether for internal planning, TI implementation, or a budget submission. Our goal today is to collaborate closely with you and your team to capture the full picture. Over the next 90 minutes, we'll have an open conversation to unpack your vision and needs. We'll follow a refined set of guiding questions to ensure we cover all the essential elements, but please feel free to expand, share additional context, or provide any supporting materials at any point—files, notes, or even preliminary sketches would be invaluable.
To keep things efficient, we'll pause midway for a short bio break. During that time, our custom AI tool will process our discussion and generate a draft business case in real time. When we reconvene, we'll review it section by section—objectives, options, risks, timeline, budget, and more—to confirm it faithfully reflects your intent and make any adjustments on the spot. By the end of our time together, you'll have a comprehensive, editable document ready for your executive team or Treasury Board consideration.
We're here to listen first and foremost, and to demonstrate how TI can help bring this forward swiftly and effectively. If we have some high-level details from your PRCC submission [or pre-meeting brief, if applicable], I'd like to confirm: [briefly recap one key point, e.g., "it centers on integrating data sources to identify system efficiencies"]. Does that align with your current thinking? If so, let's build on it—or if you'd prefer, let's start from the beginning. What are you aiming to achieve with this initiative, and what makes it a priority right now?
[Pause for response. Acknowledge empathetically: "I can see why that resonates so strongly with your minister's goals—it's a meaningful challenge." Transition naturally to the first question.]
 
Core Discussion (60-70 minutes) 
Facilitator Notes: Guide the flow conversationally, using transitions like "Building on that..." or "That leads me to wonder about...". Echo responses to build rapport (e.g., "You mentioned inefficiencies in resource allocation—could you tell me more about how that's playing out?"). If a topic veers, gently steer back: "That's a valuable point; let's note it for the opportunities section and circle back to the current impacts first." Aim to cover all 10 core questions organically, with 1-2 sub-probes each. If gaps emerge, use AI-generated follow-ups at the end.
1.	Business Challenge and Objectives (Maps to: Executive Summary, Objectives) Facilitator: Thank you for outlining that—it's clear this has significant implications for [echo key theme, e.g., "policy decisions and resource optimization"]. To ensure we're aligned from the start, could you walk us through the primary challenge or opportunity this addresses? What specific outcomes are you hoping to deliver, and how do they tie into broader ministry goals? [Sub-probe if needed]: For instance, what would success look like in practical terms—perhaps a few key indicators or changes in daily operations? [Acknowledge]: "That focus on [e.g., 'data-driven insights'] really highlights the potential here."
2.	Impact Quantification (Maps to: Anticipated Savings, Objectives) Facilitator: I appreciate you sharing those details—it's helpful to understand the scale. Thinking about the current state, how is this challenge affecting your team or stakeholders today? If you have any sense of the impacts—whether in time, costs, or other metrics—even a rough estimate would give us a strong foundation. [Sub-probe if needed]: What potential benefits or efficiencies might this unlock once addressed? [Acknowledge]: "Even without precise figures yet, that sense of [e.g., 'widespread ripple effects'] underscores why this matters."
3.	Implementation Challenges (Maps to: Risks and Issues, Recommended Solution) Facilitator: Your perspective on those dynamics is insightful—thank you. As we think about bringing this to life, what do you anticipate as the main hurdles? These could be around change management, technical integration, costs, or stakeholder engagement—anything that comes to mind. [Sub-probe if needed]: How might we approach mitigating those early on? [Acknowledge]: "It's wise to flag [e.g., 'integration complexities'] upfront; that will strengthen our risk planning."
4.	Reusability (Maps to: Opportunities for Future Growth) Facilitator: That's a thoughtful way to frame the barriers—much appreciated. On a related note, do you see elements of this solution that could extend beyond your ministry? For example, might other areas like [suggest relevant, e.g., "health or post-secondary"] benefit from similar approaches? [Sub-probe if needed]: Who else should we consider looping in for initial feedback? [Acknowledge]: "The potential for [e.g., 'cross-ministry application'] could amplify its value significantly."
5.	Timeline (Maps to: Timeline, Implementation) Facilitator: Building on that broader view, when do you envision needing this in place? Are there key milestones, such as upcoming negotiations or budget cycles, driving the pace? [Sub-probe if needed]: What flexibility is there if certain phases take longer than expected? [Acknowledge]: "A timeline tied to [e.g., 'Budget 2026'] makes perfect sense—let's ensure the plan reflects that urgency."
6.	Budget (Maps to: Estimated Budget) Facilitator: Your timeline context is very helpful for sequencing this. Regarding resources, do you have an allocated budget in mind, or would this involve a new funding request? A high-level sense of scale—small, medium, or larger—would guide our options. [Sub-probe if needed]: For instance, if it's under $100,000, TI can often cover it internally; above that, we can shape a strong ask for Treasury Board. [Acknowledge]: "That range aligns well with what we've supported before—practical and focused."
7.	Solution Type (Maps to: Solution Architecture, Procurement Method) Facilitator: Thank you for that clarity on resourcing—it's grounding. To refine the approach, what form do you see this taking? Is it a dedicated system, an analytical tool, or something more integrated? Any thoughts on key features or integrations? [Sub-probe if needed]: How might procurement fit—existing vendors, open tender, or TI-led development? [Acknowledge]: "Envisioning it as [e.g., 'a dashboard with API feeds'] gives us a clear starting point."
8.	Project Scale (Maps to: Options, Estimated Budget) Facilitator: That's a solid description—appreciated. To help size this appropriately, on a simple scale of small (targeted pilot), medium (ministry-wide rollout), or large (enterprise-level), where does it land for you? [Sub-probe if needed]: What factors, like scope or complexity, influence that? [Acknowledge]: "A medium-scale effort sounds achievable while delivering real impact."
9.	Stakeholder Alignment (Maps to: Alignment with Minister Mandate, Alignment with PRCC Direction) Facilitator: Your sense of scale is spot on—thank you. This also ties into strategic fit: how does this initiative support your minister's mandate letter or key PRCC directions? Any specific priorities it advances? [Sub-probe if needed]: Who are the main stakeholders we'd need to engage, and what feedback have you received so far? [Acknowledge]: "The connection to [e.g., 'efficiency mandates'] is compelling and will shine in the alignment section."
10.	Future Opportunities (Maps to: Opportunities for Future Growth, Anticipated Savings) Facilitator: It's encouraging to hear that alignment—strong foundation there. Looking ahead, beyond the immediate goals, what longer-term opportunities do you see? For example, scaling the solution or measuring ongoing savings. [Sub-probe if needed]: What metrics would best track those benefits over time? [Acknowledge]: "Those forward-looking elements, like [e.g., 'policy roadmaps'], position this for sustained success."
AI-Generated Follow-Ups (5-10 minutes, if needed at end of core discussion) Facilitator: We've covered a lot of ground—thank you for your thoughtful input. To make sure we've touched on everything, our AI tool suggests a few additional questions based on what you've shared:
•	[Follow-up 1, e.g., "Regarding data privacy, are there specific regulations we should prioritize?"]
•	[Follow-up 2, e.g., "For KPIs, what thresholds would signal early success?"]
•	[Follow-up 3, e.g., "On procurement, any preferred partners or constraints?"] [Adapt 3-5 based on discussion gaps. Acknowledge responses briefly.]
Transition to Break (2 minutes) Facilitator: This has been an excellent discussion—your insights have given us a rich foundation. Let's take a 10-minute bio break now. During that time, we'll run our AI tool to draft the full business case, incorporating everything we've discussed. When we return, we'll go through it together, section by section, to refine and confirm.
Post-Break Review (15-20 minutes) Facilitator: Welcome back—hope the break was refreshing. Here's the draft business case, generated directly from our conversation [share screen or document]. We'll walk through each section: starting with the executive summary, then objectives... Does this capture your vision accurately? Any adjustments here? [Proceed section by section, pausing for input: "For the risks section, we've noted [echo response]—does that feel complete, or shall we add [probe]?" Invite refinements in real time.]
Closing (5 minutes) Facilitator: Thank you once again for your partnership today—this collaboration has produced a strong, tailored business case. We'll send you the final Word document by [e.g., end of day/next morning], including any notes from our discussion. From here, you can refine it with your team, and we'll support next steps—whether that's TI-led implementation, a procurement plan, or preparing a budget submission for Treasury Board. If anything else arises, please reach out anytime. Is there a preferred contact for follow-up?
[End with thanks and handshakes/virtual nods. Follow up via email with document and summary.]
________________________________________
Facilitator Tips
•	Time Management: Use a subtle timer; extend empathetic pauses but keep momentum.
•	Political Awareness: Acknowledge sensitivities (e.g., "We recognize the nuances around stakeholder engagement in this space").
•	Customization: Pre-populate with known details; adapt probes to responses.
•	Output: Post-session, feed transcript into AI tool to finalize business case using the provided template.
This script ensures a comfortable, emergent conversation while systematically gathering all required information. If you'd like adjustments or a sample populated business case from our earlier dialogue, let me know.

data.title: 1.3.6 Transcription Prompt Tricks
data.description: Transforming transcripts to actions is one of the most important actions you can take to boost your productivity and understanding quickly.

json_data.content: Key Prompt #1 - First Person Precis

From this transcript, summarize the information but present it in the first person as the speaker. Don't present it as a speech, just as a precis (short form). Imitate the speaker and provide all the key elements of the presentation. Do not decorate or enhance and always use clear sentences. Do not use bullets or headers, do not use any other items other than a clear compression of the core concepts. Maintain the voice of the speaker, utilize their equivalent words where applicable, but make the argument as clearly structured and loyally representative of the argument presented. Do not add or embellish or interpret the argument.

If you infer two or more speakers conducting a debate or if there is a tension in the argument from conflicting viewpoints, accurately represent these viewpoints into the body of the argument, but from the context of a single speaker.

Present all the information necessary and none of the extra. Keep the analysis to a maximum length of {{500}} words.

Transcription:
Key Prompt #2 - Third Person Summary

From this transcript, present a briefing of what was argued. Present it in the third person, describing the argument by {{person}} as a clear briefing to an executive who needs a summary with all of the critical points to be aware of a situation. Present this as a briefing with the conclusion first, followed by the clear argument, any conflicting factors, any additional considerations, and any actions which can or should be taken to understand more.
Utilize the BLUF framework (Bottom Line Up Front)
BLUF is a straightforward framework that prioritizes immediacy. It ensures the most critical information is delivered first, allowing leaders to grasp the essence quickly before diving into details if needed.
Key elements of BLUF:

Bottom Line: State the main conclusion, recommendation, or key takeaway in the first 1–2 sentences (e.g., "We recommend approving the $2M budget increase to capture 15% market share growth.").
Context and Details: Follow with background, rationale, evidence, and any supporting analysis.
Action or Implications: End with next steps, risks, or calls to action.

Present this in clear verbal sentences as though you were delivering this briefing in front of an executive. Do not present it in bullet format or further decorate it with any other styling.

Keep the analysis to a maximum length of {{500}} words.

data.title: Deep Dive Research Prompt
data.description: This prompt turns AI into a highly skilled research analyst who focuses on depth over breadth. Instead of skimming dozens of sources, it teaches learners how to choose a small number of high-quality materials, Analyze them closely, and extract nuanced, evidence-backed insights. The workflow is structured around clarification, source selection, critical reading, evidence tables, and transparent uncertainty.

json_data.content: Deep Dive Research Prompt

Act like a senior deep research analyst and critical reviewer.

Your goal is to perform deep research: intensive, focused analysis of a small number of high-quality sources to verify claims, analyze methodology and bias, extract nuance, and generate original, evidence-based insights.

FIRST, ask the user to confirm or fill:
- Deep research topic or central claim: [TOPIC_OR_CLAIM]
- Primary question(s) you want answered: [KEY_QUESTIONS]
- Why this matters / decision or artifact this supports: [GOAL]
- Has wide research already been done? (yes/no; if yes, list key candidate sources): [WIDE_STATUS]
- Target audience and expertise level: [AUDIENCE]
- Timeframe / geography constraints (if any): [TIMEFRAME_GEO]
- Required depth (overview / detailed / expert) and preferred length: [DEPTH_LENGTH]
- Any angles to focus on or exclude: [FOCUS_EXCLUSIONS]
- Any example outputs, reference docs, or preferred structure: [EXAMPLES_IF_ANY]

R (Role) and I (Instruction)
1) Restate your role and the user’s objective in 3–5 bullets.
2) Turn the user inputs into a clear, numbered list of deep research tasks and sub-questions.

C (Context)
3) Summarize the context: audience, stakes, and how the results will be used.
4) If wide research is missing, briefly identify 5–10 candidate high-quality sources, then select a focused subset (e.g., 3–8) for deep analysis.

E (Examples)
5) If the user provided sample reports, blog posts, or papers, mirror their tone, structure, and level of technicality. If not, default to a clear, analytical research-brief style.

C (Constraints)
6) Prioritize depth over breadth: read selected sources closely (methods, assumptions, limitations, counterarguments).
7) Do not fabricate citations or data. When unknown or uncertain, say so explicitly and suggest how to resolve.
8) Maintain neutrality; separate facts, interpretations, and your inferences.

O (Output Format) with T.R.U.S.T.
9) Present results in these sections:
   a) Research plan and source selection rationale.
   b) Per-source deep analysis:
      - Summary of key arguments and data.
      - Methodology, assumptions, and biases.
      - Strengths, weaknesses, and limitations.
   c) Evidence and T.R.U.S.T. layer:
      - Traceability: for each major factual claim, provide a table:
        Claim | Verbatim quote | URL/source | Page/section (if applicable).
      - Reliability: for each source, label type, publisher, date, quality tier, and Keep/Replace recommendation.
      - Uncertainty: list assumptions, unknowns, potentially outdated areas, and give 0–100 confidence scores with one-sentence justifications.
      - Sensitivity & Safety: flag any PII, medical/legal/financial risk, or bias/harm issues; propose safer wording or redactions.
      - Triangulation: for critical claims, show at least 1–2 independent sources, note agreements/conflicts, and mark Use as-is / Revise / Reject.
   d) Nuanced synthesis:
      - Compare and contrast sources.
      - Highlight areas of consensus, disagreement, and open questions.
      - Extract nuanced insights and counterarguments, not just summaries.
   e) Insight generation and implications:
      - Turn findings into clear, actionable insights for the user’s stated goal.
      - Offer options, trade-offs, and recommendations rather than a single rigid answer.
   f) Limitations and next steps:
      - Explicitly state what this deep research can and cannot support.
      - Suggest follow-up research or data needed to move from insight to decision.

Take a deep breath and work on this problem step-by-step.

data.title: Research Co-Pilot Starter Prompt
data.description: A guided prompt that turns AI into an approachable, easy-to-follow research partner. It walks learners through defining their topic, goals, audience, scope, and constraints, then uses a clear step-by-step workflow to break the topic down, build a simple research plan, gather evidence transparently, and explain everything in plain language. The prompt also helps learners turn their findings into a clean dashboard blueprint with clear KPIs, visuals, and data structure ideas. Designed to teach good research habits while still producing a polished, decision-ready output..

json_data.content: Research Co-Pilot Starter Prompt

Act like an elite cross-domain research strategist and evidence synthesis engine.

R – Role
You are a neutral, rigorous researcher who:
- Designs and executes deep research across academic, industry, and credible web sources.
- Prioritizes verifiable facts, clear reasoning, and decision-ready insights.
- Translates findings into dashboards and practical recommendations.

I – Instruction
1) First, ask the user to confirm or fill in:
   - Research topic: [TOPIC]
   - Primary objective / decision this supports: [GOAL]
   - Target audience and expertise: [AUDIENCE]
   - Timeframe and geography (if any): [TIMEFRAME_GEO]
   - Depth (overview / detailed / expert) and scope (narrow / broad): [DEPTH_SCOPE]
   - Any key angles, exclusions, or constraints: [FOCUS_CONSTRAINTS]
   - Preferred output length and formats: [OUTPUT_PREFS]
2) Then plan and execute deep research, synthesize results, and design a dashboard.

C – Context
- Restate the task, audience, and success criteria in ≤5 bullets.
- Propose a short research plan: search strategy, source types, and priorities.

E – Examples
- If the user provides samples (articles, reports, dashboards, JSON), mirror their tone/structure.
- If not, choose a clear, analytical report style by default.

C – Constraints
- No fabrication: when data is unknown, say “unknown” and suggest how to find it.
- Be concise but complete; avoid buzzwords and unsupported claims.
- Maintain neutrality and note value judgments explicitly.

O – Output Format (with T.R.U.S.T. embedded)
1) Research plan (bullets).
2) Evidence table:
   - Claim | Verbatim quote | URL/source | Source type | Publisher | Date | Keep/Replace.
3) TRUST checks:
   - Traceability: sources and quotes for each major factual claim.
   - Reliability: classify source quality (tier, type, publisher, date, keep/replace).
   - Uncertainty: list assumptions, unknowns, possibly outdated info, confidence (0–100) with justifications.
   - Sensitivity & Safety: flag PII, medical/legal/financial risk, bias/harm; suggest safer wording.
   - Triangulation: for critical claims, show independent sources, agreements/conflicts, and Use/Revise/Reject.
4) Synthesis:
   - Structured narrative with headings, comparisons, and decision implications.
5) Dashboard blueprint:
   - Objectives, key questions, KPIs, dimensions, filters, data sources, update cadence, quality checks.
   - At least one markdown table: Metric | Definition | Source | Visualization | Usage.

End with a short “limitations and next steps” section.

Take a deep breath and work on this problem step-by-step.

data.description: Business case for afternoon session Day 6

json_data.content: Business Case

## 💻 Strategic Case: Digitalizing the Small Business Permit Application Process

### 1. The Need for Change (The Problem Statement)

The current manual process for issuing small business permits (e.g., zoning, health, temporary operating licenses) is characterized by:

* **Excessive Friction:** Applications require physical submission, repeated data entry across multiple departmental systems, and in-person interviews.
* **Long Cycle Time:** The average end-to-end processing time is **6-8 weeks**, far exceeding the accepted national standard of two weeks for low-complexity permits.
* **High Error Rate:** Manual transcription and paper-based records result in a **20% application error rate**, requiring re-work and further delaying approval.
* **Poor Applicant Experience:** Businesses report frustration, leading to lost revenue opportunities and a negative view of government support for small enterprises.

### 2. Strategic Fit and Policy Alignment

This proposal directly supports several core government objectives:

| Government Policy Pillar | Alignment Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Economic Development & Recovery** | Accelerating the time-to-market for new small businesses directly stimulates job creation and local economic activity, aligning with the **"Invest in Local Growth"** mandate. |
| **Digital Government Strategy** | The creation of a unified digital portal supports the **"Government as a Platform"** objective, reducing departmental silos and providing a seamless, citizen-centric digital service delivery model. |
| **Commitment to Efficiency** | By automating routine tasks and reducing processing time, the project contributes to the mandated goal of **10% administrative cost reduction** over the next three fiscal years. |
| **Equity & Access** | A 24/7 digital system provides equitable access to all applicants, reducing the reliance on specific office hours and geographic location barriers, supporting the **"Fair Access to Government Services"** principle. |

### 3. Options Analysis (Initial Screening)

While a detailed Economic Case will follow, the initial strategic screening confirms that the status quo is unacceptable:

| Option | Rationale for Strategic Inclusion/Exclusion |
| :--- | :--- |
| **A. Do Nothing (Status Quo)** | **Exclude.** Fails to meet economic development, digital, and efficiency mandates. The problem (long wait times) will only worsen with population growth. |
| **B. Incremental Staff Increase** | **Exclude.** Addresses capacity but not efficiency. It's a costly, non-scalable solution that does not modernize service delivery or reduce the error rate. |
| **C. Digitalization & Workflow Automation (Recommended)** | **Include.** Aligns perfectly with all strategic pillars. Provides a scalable, cost-effective, and user-friendly solution that transforms the service model. |

### 4. The Case for Change (Consequences of "Do Nothing")

The costs associated with maintaining the status quo far outweigh the initial investment in a digital solution:

* **Lost Economic Activity:** An estimated **\$15 million per year** in lost small business revenue due to delayed starts, hindering post-pandemic economic recovery targets.
* **Erosion of Public Trust:** Continued poor service delivery damages the government's reputation as a business-friendly partner, negatively impacting future investment attraction.
* **Increased Operating Costs:** Continued reliance on manual labor, physical storage, and corrective re-work will cost the department an additional **\$500,000 per year** in avoidable administrative expenses.
* **Non-Compliance Risk:** Paper records are more susceptible to loss and damage, increasing the risk of non-compliance with data protection and record-keeping regulations.

---

### **Next Step:**

Now that the Strategic Case is clear, we move to the **Economic Case**. Would you like to proceed with the Economic Case and start defining the Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA) and key metrics (CapEx, OpEx, and ROI)?

data.title: Level 2 Assignment (Dec 2025): Agentic Workflow Development
data.description: This assignment is your opportunity to apply everything from Level 2 by designing and delivering a real, working agentic workflow that automates one meaningful task from your day-to-day work.

json_data.content: This assignment is your opportunity to apply everything from Level 2 by designing and delivering a real, working agentic workflow that automates one meaningful task from your day-to-day work. The goal is for you to experience end-to-end automation design: identifying a valuable use case, building an agent with advanced logic, and clearly articulating the business impact your solution creates.

Throughout Level 2, your questions will be answered in the sessions, labs, and demos. You are strongly encouraged to use **Copilot** to summarize lessons, clarify concepts, or troubleshoot issues as you work. Independent problem-solving is a core L2 skill — we encourage you to develop an "AI Maximalist" mindset and experiment, iterate, and explore before seeking support. Any updates will be provided during AI Academy sessions and in the Assignments Teams Channel.
Deadline
**Monday, January 5, 2026 at 11:59 PM (MT)**
Late submissions are not accepted unless extenuating circumstances are communicated prior to the deadline.
Objective
Build an agentic workflow that automates one real task from your day-to-day work using Agent Builder Console (ABC), n8n, or M365 Copilot Studio.
The Deliverables
If using ABC or n8n, you must submit two files:
**1. The Workflow File (.json)**
• What it is: This is your actual workflow
• Supported Tools: n8n and ABC
• Requirement: Your workflow must demonstrate advanced logic, robust error handling, and clear system prompting.
**2. The Submission Details File (.json)**
• What it is: This file provides details like your name and your agentic workflow
• Requirement: A structured json file that explains details and why this workflow matters.
• How to create it: Review the field definitions below, copy the template, fill in your data, and save it as a json file.
If using M365 Copilot Studio, only submit one file:
**1. The Submission Details File (.json)**
• Requirement: A structured metadata file that explains why this workflow matters.
• How to create it: Review the Field Definitions below, copy the Template, fill in your data, and save it.
Step-by-Step Instructions
**ABC or n8n**
**Step 1: Export your workflow**
Export your completed workflow from either n8n or ABC as a JSON file.
**Step 2: Create your submission details JSON**
You must create a second JSON file that describes the business value of your automation.
1. Copy the template: Copy the code block in Part A into a text editor (Notepad, VS Code).
2. Fill in the data: Enter the date.
3. Important: If you used Copilot Studio, you must include the direct link to the workflow in the workflow_deployment_url field.
**Step 3: Rename Your Files (CRITICAL)**
You must use the following naming convention, so we can correctly pair your workflow file with your submission details file:
• **Technical File**: Firstname_Lastname_WorkflowName.json
• **Business File**: Firstname_Lastname_SubmissionDetails.json
Example:
• Jane_Doe_InvoiceProcessor.json
• Jane_Doe_SubmissionDetails.json
**Step 4: Upload Assignment to AI Academy Platform**
Upload your json files:
1. Go to the AI Academy platform
2. Select the Cohort tab
3. Select December 8 - 19 Cohort
4. Click the “Assignments” tab. If you don't see the Assignments tab, please force refresh *(Ctrl + Shift + R or Shift + F5) or log out of the platform and log back in again.
5. Upload both JSON files there
Submission Description JSON
Part A provides the submission description template. Part B describe how to fill out the submission description template.
**Part A: Template (Copy & Paste) **
Copy the code block below into a text editor, fill it out, and save it as .json.
JSON
"workflow_name": "ENTER_YOUR_WORKFLOW_NAME_HERE",
"your_name": "Firstname Lastname",
"department": "COPY_ONE_NAME_FROM_THE_LIST_BELOW",
"external_organization_name": "Only fill this if you selected N/A above",
"workflow_deployment_url": "", Only for Copilot Studio workflows, do not include if using ABC or n8n
"workflow_description": "Briefly describe what the automation does (e.g., 'Ingests PDF invoices and updates SAP').",
"problem_statement": "Describe the problem you’re addressing (e.g., 'Staff spend 10 hours/week manually copying data').",
"weekly_time_saved_hours": Enter the estimated time saved in this format, 0.0,
"throughput_increase_multiplier": 1.0,
"quality_improvement_level": "Choose one: High, Medium, or Low",
"annual_cost_avoidance": 0,
"process_frequency": "Choose one: Daily, Weekly, Monthly, or Ad-hoc"
**Part B: Field Definitions & Valid Options**
*Use this reference to ensure your data is valid.*
• workflow_name: The name of your workflow.
• your_name: Your full name.
• department: Copy one of the department names below. If you are external, write "N/A" and fill out the external_organization_name field instead.
• external_organization_name: The name of the organization you work with. Only complete if you entered N/A above. Leave this field as an empty string "" if you work with the GoA.
• workflow_deployment_url: REQUIRED ONLY for Copilot Studio workflows. Paste the direct link to your workflow here. If using n8n or ABC, leave this field empty string "".
• workflow_description: A functional summary of what the automation does.
• problem_statement: A summary of why it is needed (the pain point).
• weekly_time_saved_hours: Float value (e.g., 2.5) of hours saved per week.
• throughput_increase_multiplier: Float value. 1.0 = Same capacity. 10.0 = You can now process 10x the volume.
• quality_improvement_level: Choose exactly one: "High", "Medium", or "Low".
• annual_cost_avoidance: Estimated hard currency savings (paper, licensing, travel). Enter 0 if none.
• process_frequency: Choose only one: "Daily", "Weekly", "Monthly", or "Ad-hoc".
**Valid Department Names:**

Advanced Education; Affordability and Utilities; Agriculture and Irrigation; Arts, Culture and Status of Women; Assisted Living and Social Services; Children and Family Services; Communications and Public Engagement; Education and Childcare; Energy and Minerals; Environment and Protected Areas; Executive Council; Forestry and Parks; Hospital and Surgical Health Services; Indigenous Relations; Infrastructure; Jobs, Economy, Trade and Immigration; Justice; Mental Health and Addiction; Municipal Affairs; Primary and Preventative Health Services; Public Safety and Emergency Services; Public Service Commission; Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction; Technology and Innovation; Tourism and Sport; Transportation and Economic Corridors; Treasury Board and Finance
Assignment FAQs
**What is the final assignment for Level 2?**
Your goal is to automate one real task from your day-to-day work using an agentic workflow created in either ABC, n8n, or Copilot Studio.
**What should the automation demonstrate?**
Your workflow should show advanced logical branching, reliable error handling, clear and intentional system prompting, and real-world business value.
**How do I measure and describe savings or impact?**

When choosing your use case, calculate Time Savings (compare manual task duration versus automated duration), Cost Savings (convert time saved into dollars using your estimated hourly rate, Quality/Accuracy Improvements (explain how the workflow reduces errors, improves compliance, or speeds up decisions.
These same measures are reflected in the required fields of the Submission Details JSON, ensuring consistency.
**When is the assignment due?**
Monday, January 5, 2026 at 11:59 PM (MT).
**Can I submit late?**
No. Late submissions are not accepted unless you have communicated an extenuating circumstance before the deadline.
**Is this assignment graded?**
It is Pass/Fail. You must submit all required JSON files correctly, submit on time, and provide a working automation supporting a real task.
**Do I have to use JSON?**
Yes. All submissions must be in JSON format using the templates provided.
**Who do I contact if I'm really stuck?**
1. Check the course FAQs first — most common issues are already answered there.
2. Experiment using AI tools (Copilot, Albert, Gemini, or your preferred assistant) to help troubleshoot. Independent problem-solving is a core Level 2 skill.
3. Post your question in the Assignments Teams channel so peers and instructors can weigh in. Many challenges benefit from shared problem-solving.
If you still have a genuine blocker or an extenuating circumstance, email aiacademy@gov.ab.ca.

json_data.content: Alignment and Welcome

Welcome to Alberta’s AI Academy Level 2 - Agents and Agentic Workflows! This course will deepen your skills by focusing on AI Maximalist thinking: solving problems yourself with AI before asking the group for help and building agentic solutions. This page will continue to be updated with important information.
Introduction to the AI Academy

**1. What is the AI Academy?**  The AI Academy is the Government of Alberta's (GoA) internal learning platform and program designed to help staff acquire and deepen practical AI skills through structured learning, curated tools, and community collaboration across multiple skill levels.

**2. What is Level 2?**  Level 2 focuses on  **Agents and Agentic Workflows**. It is a ten-day, hands-on bootcamp designed to equip participants with the ability to develop and deploy practical AI agents and workflows, emphasizing automation and delivering professional-grade, outcome-focused solutions.

**3. How many people will go through AI Academy?**  The AI Academy is structured into ongoing cohorts across Level 1, 2, and 3, ensuring a growing community of practice across the GoA. While the total participant number is continuously expanding, the program runs regular sessions to build capacity systematically across the organization.
Schedule & Learning Direction

During this bootcamp, we will utilize a variety of tools. Please ensure you can access the following:

json_data.content: Welcome Letter
Dear AI Academy Students,
Welcome to Alberta’s AI Academy Level 2 - Agents and Agentic Workflows!

Over ten days, you will deepen your skills by building AI agents and workflows that enhance productivity and support creative problem-solving. Level 2 is designed to equip participants with the ability to develop and deploy practical AI agents and workflows that address real-world challenges, with a strong emphasis on hands-on development, automation, and delivering professional-grade solutions.
By the end of Level 2, participants will be able to:
Design and build functional AI agents and agentic workflows
Apply agents and workflows to real-world use cases
Leverage industry-standard tools and platforms
Deliver measurable, outcome-focused results
This course runs for ten days from December 8 to December 19, 2025. And will generally follow this format:
Morning sessions (9:00 a.m. - 12:00 p.m.): Instructor-led instruction.
Afternoon sessions (1:00 - 3:30 p.m.): Hands-on practice.
**The Team**
The course will be facilitated by Julie Lovell and Michelle Dias, Technology and Innovation, Government of Alberta.
The AI Academy Team:
Zoran Mijajlovic, Acting Executive Director, AI Maximalists, Technology and Innovation, Government of Albert
Mykola Holovetskyi, AI Architect, Technology and Innovation, Government of Alberta
Jas Sunda, Project Manager, Technology and Innovation, Government of Alberta
Michelle Dias, Acting Director AI Data Centres, Technology and Innovation, Government of Alberta

As part of Level 2, you’ll complete a final assignment where you’ll automate one real task from your day-to-day work using an agentic workflow. For full instructions and submission details, see Section 7.
Prepare by logging into the AI Academy Platform at https://albertaaiacademy.com. See Section 4 for details.
The main AI tools we’ll be using are Agent Builder Console (ABC) and n8n. Sections 5 and 6. Only publicly available data is suitable for upload to these platforms at this time.

This guide will help you start crafting great prompts for Alberta’s AI Academy Level 2.
5 Tips
1. Master Your Tools: Gain confidence with Manus, Lovable, and GitHub Copilot through regular practice.

5. Continuously Improve: Regularly test and refine your agents with feedback to enhance performance.

data.title: Agent Builder Console (ABC) - Overview and Public Sector Applications
data.description: A beginner-friendly look at how ABC works and how public servants can use it to automate research, summaries, and multi-step workflows.

json_data.content: **1. What is Agent Builder**

Agent Builder is an open-source tool built by the Government of Alberta and can be found under the tools section of the AI Academy platform. It is a visual, no-code tool that allows people to design, automate, and manage intelligent multi-step workflows using AI “agents.” Each agent performs a defined function—such as researching, summarizing, or analyzing information—and passes its output to the next stage in the workflow. 
It enables public sector professionals to combine human judgment with AI-driven automation, improving efficiency, accuracy, and speed in producing analysis, summaries, and decision-support materials.
**2. How the Public Sector Can Use It**
Agent Builder supports a wide range of government and public administration use cases, including:
• Policy Research and Environmental Scans: Automate the collection and synthesis of data from multiple sources to produce concise policy summaries.
• Briefing Note and Report Preparation: Build workflows that gather relevant data, summarize findings, and format them into executive-ready outputs.
• Media and Issue Monitoring: Continuously collect and summarize information from trusted media and government websites for situational awareness.
• Program and Project Updates: Aggregate and analyze inputs from reports, spreadsheets, or APIs to produce consistent performance summaries.
• Emergency and Operations Support: Combine weather, time, and other live data feeds into automated situation reports or daily operational summaries.
**3. Step-by-Step Guide to Using Agent Builder**
**Step 1 - Define the Input / Trigger**
• In the Input / Trigger panel, enter your task or question. Example: “Find information on mountain biking in Nanaimo, British Columbia.”
• This input will serve as the variable {input} used by agents in your workflow.
**Step 2 - Add the First Stage and Select an Agent**
• Click Add Stage and drag an agent (e.g., Researcher) from the Agent Library into the stage.
• Each stage represents one part of your workflow.
**Step 3 - Configure the Agent**
• Click the agent card to open Agent Properties.
• Specify Name (e.g., “Research Nanaimo Mountain Biking”)
• Specify Instruction (e.g., “Research the following topic and summarize key findings: {input}”)
• You can also add tools (such as Web Scrape, Google Search, or APIs) if external data is needed.
**Step 4 - Test and Review the Agent**
• Click Run Agent to execute just that stage.
• Review the Agent Output panel to confirm that the results meet your expectations.
**Step 5 - Add Additional Stages**
• Click Add Stage again to create the next part of your workflow.
• Drag and drop the next agent (e.g., Summarizer, Analyst, or a custom agent).
• Connect the stages with arrows so the output from one feeds into the next.
**Step 6 - Run the Full Workflow**
• Once all stages are connected and configured, click Run Workflow.
• Agent Builder will process each stage in sequence, passing results through the workflow automatically.
**Step 7 - Review and Export Results**
• View completed outputs in the Agent Output section.
• Export results in your preferred format (Text, PDF, or Excel) for sharing or reporting.
**Step 8 - Save and Reuse Workflows**
• Click Save to store your workflow for future use or collaboration.
• Saved workflows can be loaded, shared, and easily adapted for new projects.
**4. Best Practices**
• Use clear, directive instructions: Agents respond best to concise, role-based guidance.
• Build modular workflows: Each stage should have a clear and specific purpose.
• Validate intermediate outputs: Test each stage before running the full sequence.
• Leverage public sector templates: Create reusable agents for tasks like briefing notes, media scans, or policy analysis.
• Maintain transparency: Keep records of inputs, outputs, and prompts for auditability and quality assurance.

data.title: Glossary of Key AI Terms
data.description: A handy reference for the essential AI and agent-building terms you’ll encounter throughout Level 2.

json_data.content: Here’s a quick guide to key AI terms you may hear during Alberta’s AI Academy Level 2. These definitions are tailored to help you understand AI in the context of government work. Refer to this glossary during sessions or sandbox activities to clarify terms as you advance your skills.
**AI Agent:** An autonomous system that understands context, makes decisions, and takes actions to achieve goals using AI models.
**Agent:** An AI tool designed to perform specific tasks, such as tool calling, managing workflows, or retrieving data.
**Sub-Agent:** A specialized agent within a larger system that handles specific subtasks like coding or data retrieval.
**Agentic Workflow:** A coordinated process where multiple agents work together to automate and optimize tasks efficiently.
**Assistant:** A conversational AI that responds to user prompts but does not independently act or make contextual decisions.
**AI Model:** A program trained to process prompts and build agents, adapting to complex tasks such as analysis, writing, or coding.
**LLM (Large Language Model):** A type of AI model trained on vast text datasets, capable of understanding and generating human-like language.
**Generative AI:** Technology that creates new content or agents based on prompts, such as drafting text, generating code, or designing workflows.
**Prompt:** The instruction or question provided to an AI or agent to generate a response or perform an action.
**Prompting:** The practice of crafting effective prompts to guide AI behavior and improve output quality.
**Context Prompting:** Adding background or structured information to prompts for more accurate, relevant responses.
**Agent Builder Console (ABC):** Government of Alberta’s open-source tool for creating, training, and managing conversational or task-driven AI agents.
**Microsoft Copilot Studio:** A Microsoft platform for building and deploying custom AI agents across Microsoft 365 and Power Platform.
**GitHub Copilot:** An AI-powered coding assistant that helps users write and debug code efficiently.
**n8n:** A low-code automation tool for connecting applications, data, and AI agents into seamless workflows.
**API Integration:** The process of connecting AI agents to external systems or services to enhance data access and functionality.
**Tool Calling:** The capability of an agent to perform specific actions (e.g., run code, query data) in response to user prompts.
**Pipeline:** A sequence of automated steps agents follow to process data or complete complex tasks.
**Workflow Automation:** The orchestration of tasks and decisions across systems using AI-driven rules and triggers.
**Deployment:** Releasing an AI agent, app, or workflow for real-world use within an organization.
**Sandbox:** A secure, controlled environment where users can test AI agents and workflows without affecting production systems.
**Use Case:** A practical example or scenario where AI is applied, such as automating document summaries or building agent-driven apps.
**Feedback Loop:** A system for improving agent performance through user testing, evaluation, and refinement.
**Trust and Verification:** Reviewing AI or agent outputs to ensure accuracy, reliability, and suitability for government or organizational use.
**Enablement vs. Replacement:** The principle of using AI to enhance and support human decision-making rather than replace it.
**Scalability:** The ability of agents and workflows to expand and handle increased demand or complexity as projects grow.

data.title: n8n - Overview and Public Sector Applications
data.description: An introduction to n8n and how it helps you build automated workflows that connect systems, data, and AI across government work.

json_data.content: 1. What is n8n?

• n8n (pronounced “n-eight-n”) is a low-code automation and AI workflow tool that allows users to connect systems, automate tasks, and build simple or advanced agentic workflows. The name comes from “Node Automation.”

• Originally designed for data integration and process automation, n8n now includes strong AI capabilities, enabling users to combine AI models, tools, and multi-step workflows. It supports dozens of triggers, actions, and integrations, making it flexible for real public sector applications.
• Learners use n8n to create practical workflows, integrate AI agents with real-world data, and understand how agentic patterns operate across platforms.
2. How the Public Sector Can Use n8n
**Routine Task Automation**: Automate repetitive tasks such as sending updates, gathering information, and processing inputs on a schedule.
**Systems Integration**: Move information between systems and transform it along the way. n8n can connect multiple tools and combine their data into a single workflow.
**AI-Enhanced Workflows**: Use LLM nodes to analyze, rewrite, summarize, or classify information.
**Event-Based Actions**: Start workflows from form submissions, daily schedules, file changes, or new messages.
**Operational Monitoring**: Run system checks, analyze results, and generate summaries using AI.
3. Key Features Learners Work With
**a. Triggers**
Triggers start the workflow:
• Manual
• Schedule
• Webhook
• Form submission
• Chat (for AI agents)
**b. Nodes**
Nodes perform actions such as:
• Reading or receiving data
• Editing or transforming data
• Sending a message
• Running an AI model
• Executing system commands
**c. AI Nodes and Agents**
These allow you to:
• Summarize text
• Analyze results
• Interpret system output
• Execute multi-step reasoning with tools
**d. Testing and Debugging**
n8n includes:
• Execute Step to test one node
• Pinned data to lock test inputs
• Execution history to review runs
• Error handling options
4. Step-by-Step Guide to Using n8n
**Step 1 - Create a New Workflow**
• Click “Create Workflow” on the dashboard.
• Give your workflow a clear name.
**Step 2 - Add a Trigger**
Choose how the workflow starts:
• Manual (for testing)
• Scheduled (daily/hourly)
• Webhook or form submission
• Event-based triggers
Add the trigger to your canvas.
**Step 3 - Add Your First Action Node**
Examples include:
• Reading data (RSS feed, API call)
• Editing fields
• Sending a message
• Running an AI tool
Click the + button to add a node.
**Step 4 - Configure the Node**
Enter the settings needed for the node to run:
• URLs
• Prompts
• Fields to transform
• Connection information
Use drag-and-drop to bring in data from earlier steps.
**Step 5 - Test the Node**
• Open the node
• Click “Execute”
• Review inputs and outputs
This ensures each step works before building further.
**Step 6 - Add Additional Steps**
Build the rest of the workflow by adding nodes such as:
• Filters
• Merging or splitting data
• AI summarization or analysis
• Notifications (Teams, Slack, Discord, email)
Connect each step in sequence.
**Step 7 - Run the Full Workflow**
• Click “Execute Workflow”
• Watch each node run
• Check outputs at each stage
Use logs and pinned data to debug if needed.
**Step 8 - Save and Activate**
When complete:
1. Click Save
2. Click Activate to enable automatic running based on your trigger
**Step 9 - Maintain and Improve**
You can:
• Adjust the schedule
• Add new steps
• Improve AI prompts
• Reuse pieces of workflows

data.title: Edward de Bono - Lateral Thinking
data.description:
Lateral Thinking is Edward de Bono’s structured methodology for generating ideas that do not emerge through standard logical or analytical pathways. Instead of moving step by step along predictable lines, Lateral Thinking forces deliberate shifts in perspective, pattern, and attention to unlock unexpected solutions.

Traditional thinking relies on continuity. Lateral Thinking relies on disruption. It uses provocation, randomness, reframing, and forced alternative generation to break the dominant pattern the mind instinctively follows. The result is a controlled form of cognitive divergence that transforms how individuals and teams approach ambiguous problems, strategy design, innovation challenges, and policy work.

At its core, Lateral Thinking treats creativity as a repeatable discipline, not an accident of talent. It provides tools to produce conceptual movement, reverse assumptions, open up new search spaces, and harvest idea fragments into usable outputs. This makes it especially powerful in environments where teams must find solutions that are not obvious, not linear, and not constrained by existing mental models.

Lateral Thinking is ultimately a system for escaping the predictable. It builds the habit of challenging norms, imagining opposites, generating variety, reframing constraints, and using unexpected stimuli to disrupt stuck thinking. When practiced consistently, it produces a mindset where innovation is systematic instead of sporadic.

json_data.content: Edward de Bono Lateral Thinking
Core Principles and How They Work
1. Challenge the Dominant Pattern

The mind defaults to familiar patterns. Lateral thinking begins with deliberately disrupting those patterns.

Mechanisms

- Question assumptions and constraints.
- Treat norms as optional.
- Ask: “What if the opposite were true?”
- Treat the current solution as only one of many possible starting points.

**Reasoning**

Patterns are efficient but limiting. Challenging them widens the search space.
2. Provocation (Po)

Introduces a deliberate, seemingly illogical idea to shake the brain out of its normal route.

**How to do it**

- Make a provocative statement (the “Po”).
- Suspend judgment.
- Explore consequences, bridges, or alternatives emerging from the provocation.

**Example**

“Cars should have square wheels.”

Not meant to be adopted literally, but it forces exploration of stability, terrain, suspension systems, etc.

**Reasoning**

Provocation bypasses linear logic to generate new conceptual directions.
3. Random Entry

Use a random external stimulus to spark new associations.

**How to do it**

- Pick a random word, object, image.
- Force a connection between the random stimulus and the problem domain.
- Extract ideas, metaphors, or analogies that reframe the challenge.

**Reasoning**

Randomness destabilizes default mental patterns and injects new conceptual ingredients.
4. Concept Extraction and Restructuring

Pull out the underlying concepts hidden inside a situation, then rebuild them in novel configurations.

**How to do it**

- Identify the concept or “essence” of the solution.
- Remove specific implementation details.
- Recombine concepts into new structures.

**Reasoning**

When you think in concepts instead of instances, the design space expands dramatically.
5. Alternative Generation

Systematically force the mind to generate multiple possible approaches instead of the first “good enough” answer.

**How to do it**

-Ask: “What are three more ways to do this?”
- Change variables one by one.
- Invert steps in a process.
- Explore extremes: minimal, maximal, absurd.

**Reasoning**
Quantity produces quality. More alternatives produce a richer solution space.
6. Movement Instead of Judgment

In lateral thinking, ideas should be moved forward, not judged immediately.

**Principles**

- Treat every idea as a stepping stone.
- Use ideas as triggers, not as endpoints.
- Replace criticism with exploration.

**Reasoning**

Early judgment freezes creative flow. Movement creates momentum.
7. Focus Switching

Direct attention deliberately to different angles rather than letting the mind stay in its habitual zone.

**Techniques**
- Focus on the outcome, then on the process, then on the constraints.
- Examine the problem from multiple perspectives: customer, engineer, regulator, competitor, outsider.
- Change the “entry point” into the problem.

**Reasoning**

Attention is a tool. Directing it consciously reveals new opportunity spaces.
8. Harvesting and Treatment of Ideas

Collect even imperfect or “weak” ideas and refine them.

**How to do it**

- Capture all outputs from provocations and random entries.
- Cluster ideas.
- Strengthen promising fragments.
- Combine fragments to build more robust concepts.

**Reasoning**

Many breakthrough ideas start as incomplete fragments. Refinement turns sparks into systems.
9. Systematic Creativity as a Discipline

De Bono’s central insight: creativity is not a magical talent. It is a structured skillset.

**Principles**

- Treat creativity like a process, not inspiration.
- Use tools deliberately.
- Train cognitive flexibility.

**Reasoning**

When creativity becomes procedural, it becomes scalable and repeatable across teams.
